blocks.text: The hidden cost of bad asset management

When you manage projects, your files represent the state of the work. If a team member cannot find the latest version of an After Effects project file, the entire timeline slips. This is not just annoying. It is expensive. You spend roughly 30 percent of your day just trying to find where things live. This fragmentation causes burnout and makes you want to quit. You are forced to recreate work that already exists because the original file is buried in a deep folder structure.

The problem usually starts with shadow systems. When your official tools are hard to use, you and your team start using Slack or email to share files. These files disappear into chat history. They lose their context. You get a file named final_v2_new.aep and have no idea what changed. This happens because most systems lack a strategy. You rely on folders, but folders are static. They do not tell you the status of the asset inside.

Stop renaming files with version numbers like final_final. Instead, use a consistent naming convention that includes the date and a status code. Keep your project folders flat to reduce the depth you have to click through in the Finder.
blocks.title: Use better naming

items: Create a single source of truth. Pick one cloud location for all project assets.
Use metadata tags. In the Finder, select a file, press ⌘ I, and add tags to make files searchable by project type.
Automate your folder structure. Use a standard template for every new project to keep things consistent.
Use local tools to index your files. Apps like NeoFinder can help you search across multiple drives without opening every folder.
